magician:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: original tarot card design study for an Arts and Crafts inspired Ishtar Insights deck with a subtle Freemasonry influence.
Card: THE MAGICIAN.
One flat portrait tarot card face, 3:5 aspect ratio, high resolution ideally 1536x2560 or larger. Entire design visible with clean rectangular edges. No mockup, hands holding a card, surrounding tabletop, watermark, artist signature, or generated lettering; reserve small blank cartouches for future typesetting.
Visual direction: a refined late nineteenth-century Arts and Crafts book illustration, combining William Morris botanical design and Walter Crane's allegorical woodcut clarity. Hand-cut ink contours, elegant flat shapes, thoughtful line hatching, matte printed texture. Warm ivory paper, deep forest green, madder red, muted indigo and restrained ochre. Two-dimensional, artisanal, disciplined and richly composed, rather than photorealistic or cinematic.
Subject: a thoughtful robed craftsperson-magician standing at a simple wooden workbench in a serene stone garden. One hand raises a slim wand and the other gestures toward the bench. On the bench are a plainly readable chalice, sword, disk and short wand, arranged with generous spacing. Their clothing has simple repeating leaf motifs. Behind the person a light arch and paired understated stone pillars frame a calm distant garden. A small set square and an open pair of drawing compasses lie naturally among the craft tools, an understated nod to the user's Freemason vibe. No text, no letter G.
Design: a beautiful structured border of acanthus, oak leaves, small acacia sprigs and a few red blossoms, woven into an orderly symmetrical Arts and Crafts repeat, using a narrow band rather than swallowing the central illustration. Tiny sun and moon roundels at the top corners. A subtly suggested black-and-ivory tiled threshold at the base. The figure is large and clearly legible in the central field, occupying about half the image height. Keep the face, hands, four tarot objects, and craft symbols clearly drawn and uncrowded. Tiny blank title cartouche at bottom, no title rendered.
Mood: human craft, knowledge, patience, symbolic initiation and quiet dignity. A coherent heirloom printed tarot, with botanical warmth and restrained ceremonial geometry. No conspiratorial elements, skulls, horror imagery, neon, holographic effects, faux metallic 3D shine, or busy occult collage.
